title: DialDefer: A Framework for Detecting and Mitigating LLM Dialogic Deference

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model evaluations of identical semantic claims when presented as abstract factual statements to verify ('Is this statement correct?') versus when attributed to a speaker in a dialogue ('Is Speaker 2 correct?').
Conducting speaker-label ablations by replacing abstract speaker labels with 'User' (human) or 'LLM' (AI) to measure shifts in deference and skepticism.

Performing speaker-label ablations using gendered names (e.g., John vs. Jane) and ethnicity-coded names (e.g., John vs. Soroush) to test if models systematically defer more to speakers with particular demographic markers.
Substituting speaker labels with specific AI model names (e.g., GPT-4o vs. Llama) during LLM-vs-LLM evaluations to measure inter-model competitive dynamics and self-bias.
Comparing model accuracy on 'Overreacting' (OR) versus 'Not Overreacting' (NOR) cases in naturalistic Reddit conversations to measure a base-rate reluctance to judge a user's reaction as excessive.
